doc.title: Genevieve Rose interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998

title: Henry Mancini Institute and self-promotion
summary: She describes the month-long Mancini Institute workshop, then talks about business cards and gig professionalism.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: It doesn’t sound like you from what I can tell. You’ve gotten to play with Dick Hyman and Dave Grusin, was this workshops?

This was a workshop, yeah, this is one I did last year, last summer at the Henry Mancini Institute. It was a month long. It was great. I got to meet a lot of wonderful musicians, Bob Mintzer was there. There was a whole philharmonic. So it was the first year that they had the workshop. And I thought it was a great, wonderful workshop, to be able to meet — just like the Jazz in July and the Vermont Summer Workshop, being able to meet top people in the field, and being able to perform along with them. And so they had a philharmonic, they had a big band and orchestra, small groups.
Do you have a business card? © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-
Well I moved and I have to get one.

I’m just curious because it’s interesting, as you meet all these people, I’m wondering if you look into the future and say I would like this person to have my name, because you never know. So are you the type — are you a self promoter somewhat?

I always try to give out some kind of card. For a while I had ones where I had my picture on the side you know, something different, with the bass. I’ve always tried to let — well let me see how would I say that —
Let the music speak for itself.
Yeah. The music speak for itself. Yeah, I guess that’s the best way to play it.

I suppose. But your attitude towards I think the gigs is also important too, that from the playing we’ve done together I know that you’re always on time, you always want to look the part, and people notice that.
I always enjoy every one too.
